messages:
maria: Heads up — starting ~1968001000 we saw a KV prefix hit-rate drop on prod GPU pool A. latency p95 for gen routes went from ~85ms -> 420ms. Observed at the same time as the autoscale policy tweak that landed earlier today.

maria: perf-bot posted this:
perf-bot: prefix_hit_rate: 78% -> 12% (10:00 -> 10:03)
perf-bot: request_latency_p95: 85ms -> 420ms

devin: who rolled the autoscale tweak? I saw a config PR earlier but thought it was canaried.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T09:58 by zach — autoscale/queue_pressure-adjustment v2.1.4 applied to pool GPUs-A (canary->global).

zach: that was me. The change lowers target utilization from 72% to 60% and bumped shard rebalancing aggressiveness. I can revert if that's the likely cause.

tanya: quick check: does the KV eviction rate or shard move count spike match the time window? I can run prefix-ownership dump.

maria: eviction counter and prefix-move logs show a big burst:
```
kv.evictions_total: 1.2M @ 10:02
kv.prefix_moves: 43k between 10:01-10:04
kv.mem_usage_gb: +18% on many hosts
```

devin: hmm that suggests churn caused lots of small prefixes to miss and re-prime the KV cache. Also saw many small allocations in runtime profiler (rapid kernel fallback to slower path).

maria: profiling snippet from runtime at 10:03:
```
# top hot stacks
runtime::handle_request -> kernel_selector::fallback -> quant_path::copy_kv -> alloc_fragment
mostly waiting in memcpy + cache miss path
```

zach: the rebalancer moves prefixes by transferring ownership; we didn't coordinate TTL/priming flags. When ownership changes we set a soft-ttl to avoid double-priming, but looks like the new rebalancer aggressiveness removed that pause window so everything got evicted on the target and had to re-prime under load.

tanya: if keys are re-priming under concurrent traffic we get thundering re-populate — that's consistent with the latency spike. What do you see for per-prefix prime QPS?

maria: ran a quick query against metrics: many prefixes went from 0->300 primes/sec. Example: prefix "chat:ctx:v2" prime_rate peaked at 260/s.

devin: Other clue: kernel selection telemetry shows an increase in fallback invocations. When cold KV cache causes longer sequences we hit different kernel paths and more memory churn. So two amplifiers: eviction churn + kernel path mismatch.

zach: rollback option: revert autoscale tweak and restore old rebalancer smoothing config. I can push a revert to canary now. Anyone object?

tanya: do it. Also add a temporary rate-limiter on prefix re-primes (soft) and enable priming backoff flag. We have a helper script: prime_backoff_enable.sh

maria: running ops script to patch priming backoff and revert autoscale canary to 72% target on GPUs-A canary subset.

opsbot: action started: apply_config_patch -> autoscale.target_utilization = 72%; rebalancer.smoothing = 0.15; priming.backoff = enabled

maria: after patch, within ~90s hit-rate rebounded: perf-bot posted updated metrics:
perf-bot: prefix_hit_rate: 12% -> 70% (10:05 -> 10:07)
perf-bot: request_latency_p95: 420ms -> 95ms

devin: nice. We should still follow up: root cause is change in rebalancing aggressiveness + missing priming/backoff coordination. Add a guard in the rebalancer: if moving > N prefixes in Xs, set a coordinated soft-ttl and stagger moves.

zach: agreed. I'll open a PR with two things: revert in canary + rebalancer rate-limits and an integration test that simulates high-churn rebalances.

tanya: also add a telemetry alert when prefix_move_rate > 1k/min or when prefix_prime_rate suddenly spikes 10x. We had only infra+latency alarms but not this specific signal.

maria: created follow-up checklist:
- revert autoscale globally until fix is merged (zach)
- rebalancer guard + integration test (zach)
- add prime-rate and move-rate alerts (tanya)
- postmortem and performance profile attached to incident (maria)

zach: pushing canary revert now, will monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy revert started: autoscale-revert-2026-03-18T10:06 by zach -> canary

perf-bot: short tail p95 trend: 95ms at 10:09 (down from 420ms). KV evictions trending down to baseline.

maria: thanks all. We'll keep this thread for the postmortem notes. I'll attach heap+kv dumps to the incident doc once sanitized.

tanya: FYI I found one corner: quantized-model path uses a different priming key format. Rebalancer move logic assumed canonical keys and skipped canonicalization so those prefixes got double-evicted. I'll include a small test in the PR.

devin: good catch. small follow-up: add a perf regression test that runs kernel-selection under cold-cache and ensures fallback ratio < 5% at target loads.

maria: noted. Closing active mitigation; keeping thread open for postmortem edits. :white_check_mark:
